title: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:56Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Both bank cards are broader perimeter-and-area cards written for senior courses, covering sectors, trapezia and parallelograms, so their depth does not fit a Year 8 point focused on composite shapes.

draft.title: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
card: A composite shape is made from simple shapes joined together. Split it into rectangles and triangles, find each area, then add them. A triangle's area is ½ × base × height.
Sometimes it is easier to start with a larger shape and subtract the part that is missing, such as a corner cut out.
For the perimeter, add only the lengths along the outside edge. Lines you drew to split the shape are not part of it. Find missing sides by adding or subtracting known sides.
Example: a 10 m by 6 m rectangle has a 4 m by 3 m corner cut out. Area = 60 − 12 = 48 m². The outside edges are 10, 3, 4, 3, 6 and 6, so the perimeter is 32 m.
draft.remember: Area: add the parts or subtract the cut-out. Perimeter: trace the outside edge only.

a.q: A shape is a rectangle 6 m wide and 4 m tall, with a triangle on top. The triangle has a base of 6 m and a height of 2 m. What is the total area?
a.why: The rectangle is 6 × 4 = 24 m² and the triangle is ½ × 6 × 2 = 6 m², so the total is 30 m². Using 6 × 2 = 12 m² for the triangle gives 36 m², but that forgets the half.
a.clue: Find each part separately, then add.

b.q: Sam's room is a 9 m by 7 m rectangle with a 3 m by 2 m corner missing, which makes an L shape. What is the perimeter of the room?
b.why: Tracing the outside edge gives 9, 5, 3, 2, 6 and 7, which total 32 m. Leaving out the two edges of the notch gives 27 m, but those edges are part of the outside of the room.
b.clue: Trace every outside edge, including the notch.

check.summary: No problems found. The card example and both answers check out: 30 m² for question a and 32 m² for question b.
